text:
maria_g: Heads-up — eu-central1 batch launches are failing to allocate GPUs for ~45m. Loader logs show 'scratch read checksum mismatch' and janitor scrub spikes. Posting snippets.

maria_g: [loader] ERROR checksum mismatch: blk=0x7f8a1e size=4096 expected=0x3a9f2b ... actual=0x3a8f2b
maria_g: journal tail:
```
2024-11-01T10:22:03Z loader[pid=1234] ERROR scratch_read failed: checksum_mismatch
2024-11-01T10:22:05Z janitor[pid=4321] INFO scrub rate=120MB/s active=6
```

infra-bot: Alert: storage.read.checksum >= 0.12% (eu-central1) — triggered at 2024-11-01T10:20Z :rotating_light:

kevin_s: which node pool? instance types? seen similar on older firmware?

maria_g: impacted nodes: gnode-ec1-012, gnode-ec1-013, gnode-ec1-014, gnode-ec1-015. All are p4d-like with local NVMe scratch. IOPS reported at ~95% read queue depth; scrub concurrency jumped after last cleanup window.

sasha: can you paste fw versions and nvme smart? run:
```
nvme list && nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
nvme error-log /dev/nvme0n1 | tail -n 30
```
also try md5 of a known artifact on scratch to confirm corruption: `md5sum /scratch/artifacts/xyz` and compare to s3 copy.

jordan_ops: mitigation plan (immediate):
- cordon the 4 nodes: `kubectl cordon gnode-ec1-012 ...`
- drain non-critical batch pods: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force ...`
- reduce janitor concurrency: `janitor.max_concurrency=2` (hotfix via configmap)
- throttle scrubber: `scrubber.rate_limit=20MB/s`
- add scheduler temporary policy to avoid eu-central1 for batch: tweak `scheduler.allowed_regions`

jordan_ops: I'll push the configmap PR and a one-line patch to the scheduler now. :wrench:

lee: long-term options: firmware drift across a subset of drives vs emergent bad sectors. Replacing drives across 4 nodes (~16 NVMe modules) ~costly and lead time 2-3 weeks. Firmware rollout safer but needs canary. Suggest:
- schedule firmware update for a 6-node canary in eu-west first
- if canary green, roll with 2-node batches
Cost tradeoff: replacing now vs potential SLA hit if batch failures persist. I'll sync with procurement.

ops-oncall: short-term traffic steering: shift non-urgent batch to us-west1 & eu-west1 for 12-24h; bump preemptible capacity there. Set autoscaler cooldowns longer to avoid immediate churn.

kevin_s: any sign of SMART read_uncorrectable or media errors? if yes, we should RMA drives. if not, scrub algorithm/regression is suspect.

maria_g: nvme smart logs from gnode-ec1-012 attached in thread (snippet):
```
SMART/Health Information (NVMe specific)
critical_warning: 0
temperature: 46 C
data_units_read: 1,234,567
media_errors: 2
num_err_logs: 14
```

maria_g: media_errors > 0 on 012/013, 0 on 014/015. So looks like mixed signal.

sasha: agree with canary firmware first. Also recommend capturing dd read of affected blocks to a file and run `cmp` against S3 object to local-verify before RMA.

jordan_ops: rolled out hotfix configmap, throttles in place. cordoned 012/013 and drained low-priority pods. moving higher priority spikes to us-west.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-4423 (storage-checksum-drift-eu-central) — responders: @jordan_ops @maria_g @sasha

maria_g: next steps: 1) monitor error rate for 2h 2) schedule firmware canary tomorrow 3) open RMA if media_errors increase 4) review janitor window logic to avoid concurrent heavy scrubs during batch launches

lee: I'll draft cost/risks note for leadership — include RMA capex vs SLA exposure. Targeting decision EOD.

ops-oncall: will keep traffic steering until error rate < 0.01% for 6h. Ping me if we need region-level failover.

maria_g: thanks team. keeping thread updated. :thumbsup:
